tasks.title: Everglade: edit mode for admins
tasks.body:
The owner: "I am the owner of Everglade, so why do I not have edit mode here? Whenever a user is an admin, they need to have edit mode." An admin (a key in coax/web/api/admins.conf, logged in at /login or signing NIP-98) gets the Haunted House's edit mode in Everglade: B or EDIT, a hotbar of things to place, the picked thing's row (LEFT RIGHT AWAY NEAR TURN BIGGER SMALLER DELETE), UNDO, REDO, DONE, and ORIGINAL to go back to the designed city. The edits are the realm's published world on the server (/api/playtest/world/everglade), checked there: only an admin writes them; everyone sees them, nobody else gets edit mode. Each edit is held to the plan (not in a wall, the woods or out of the world) and DONE walks the city again (plan.coax reachability) and warns the admin of anything blocked. Then every other realm without edit mode, or a recorded reason it has none.

Plan: `docs/verse/everglade.md`.
acceptance: An admin sees EDIT in Everglade and places, moves, turns, resizes and removes things; UNDO, REDO, DONE and ORIGINAL work
The edits persist on the server for everyone; a non-admin sees them and has no EDIT
coax/web/api/test.sh: an admin's edits are saved; a non-admin's and a signed-out write are refused
DONE warns when an edit blocks a door, a character, a street node or a gate
coax test passes on the files touched

tasks.title: The Sandbox's one-sentence set pieces
tasks.body:
In the Sandbox a visitor types one sentence ("a flock of birds follows me", "a ring of blue lanterns") and the world gets that set piece. No keyword matching: the sentence goes to a server endpoint (POST /api/playtest/sandbox/piece) where Gemini on Vertex picks one piece from a fixed typed catalogue (a flock of birds that follows you, a ring of lanterns, a grove of trees, a pond) and its bounded parameters (count, kind, colour, size), checked against the catalogue on the server and again on the page. A seeded generator in Coax lays the piece out in front of you; it is one undo step and one publish in the Sandbox's build and publish model, and the Sandbox's own engine (verse/haunt.coax) draws it, the flock flying round whoever is walking.

Plan: `docs/verse/realms-port.md`.
acceptance: Coax #tests for the catalogue's validation and the seeded generator of every piece
API checks (coax/web/api/test.sh) for the endpoint against a fake model, and one check against the real model
On /realm/sandbox a typed sentence makes its piece, Z takes it back in one step, and it is published to the shared Sandbox

tasks.title: Rulesets a realm opts into: SRD 5e in Everglade
tasks.body:
The owner: "we need D&D ruleset spells like thats a ruleset some worlds can have." A realm opts into a ruleset in realms.json (`"ruleset": "srd5"`); the page carries it (data-ruleset, the page facts' ruleset= line) and the realm reads it. A shared Coax module, `verse/rules/srd5.coax`: seeded dice, the spell definitions (level, range, area, damage type and dice, save), objects' armor class and hit points by material and size (SRD 5.2.1 Breaking Objects), damage types with objects' immunities, resistance and vulnerability, and the conditions the spells need. A realm without a ruleset gets none of it. Everglade opts in.

Previous engine: `verse/everglade/previous/destructible-buildings.md` (Damage model), `0b401561a0^:crates/verse-world/src/spells/dice.rs`.
acceptance: realms.json ruleset reaches the page; Everglade says srd5 and other realms say nothing
verse/rules/srd5.coax checks: dice are seeded and in range, the object table matches the SRD, immunities hold
coax test passes on the files touched

Number keys pick a spell, a click or tap at a target casts it, Esc or right click cancels; a ring shows where it lands. Falling meteors with fire trails, impact flash, scorch and smoke; a branching bolt from the clouds with a flash. The bar in today's UI: few buttons, short words.

tasks.title: Everglade breaks: kit pieces with object hit points, chunks with physics, structural collapse
tasks.body: The owner: "everglade must be destructible like it was in previous engine." Every kit piece of the town (walls, posts, roofs, gables, doors, windows, the palisade, stalls, crates, barrels, fences, furniture) has the ruleset's object armor class and hit points. At zero it breaks into chunks that fall with rigid-body physics and settle as debris; what it held up falls (upper storeys need the section under them, a roof its walls: `verse/everglade/previous/destructible-buildings.md`, Everglade's town). Budgets keep the frame rate (chunks capped, sleep, a phone tier). Nothing a player breaks is shared; a broken building grows back after 60 s of rest with you 30 m away, and R rebuilds the town at once.
acceptance: A spell at a cottage breaks its walls into chunks and the roof falls
Chunks sleep on the ground; at most the budget's chunks live
R and regrowth stand the town back up

tasks.body: Each sentence of the owner's log said on production through the page's own path (heard words to the selector, the page does the edit): pumpkins on the stall, a building in front, the barrel bigger, 12 benches around, the crates moved, the temple hidden, a field of purple flowers. Shots kept; the world put back as it was afterwards.
acceptance: Each logged sentence does what was asked on production
edit_live.sh covers them

tasks.title: Fairy Forest: creature moods at a glance and passing remarks
tasks.body:
Every creature shows its mood at a glance: a small expression on its face and a mood glyph over its head (happy, worried, lost, hungry, tired), changing as you help. Passing close, it says a short line in a bubble, never twice in a row.

Plan: `verse/fairy-forest/README.md`.
acceptance: Each creature's glyph and face match its mood; helping it turns both happy
Passing a creature shows a short remark bubble
Desktop and phone shots

tasks.title: Make your fairy, and the mirror pool
tasks.body:
Before you wake, make your fairy: body, skin, hair, face, outfit and wings (shape, colour, glow), each a row of choices with a live preview. The look is saved per player. A mirror pool in Mossbank brings the maker back any time.

Plan: `verse/fairy-forest/README.md`.
acceptance: First visit opens the maker; DONE wakes you with that look
Reload keeps the look
The mirror pool opens the maker again

tasks.title: Your home grows room by room
tasks.body:
Your home starts as a hollow under a root in Mossbank. Rooms open one by one as you restore the forest (bed of moss, table, shelves, garden, mirror pool), and you place, move, turn and size its pieces with the shared edit tools (verse/edit). Saved per player.

Plan: `verse/fairy-forest/README.md`.
acceptance: Restoring a glade opens a new room
Pieces placed in the home stay after reload

tasks.title: A garden that grows over real days
tasks.body:
Plant seeds in your garden plot; water and sing to them. Plants grow over real days from the time planted, and the one you care for most changes into something rarer (a sapling into a glowing tree, a flower into a moon flower). Saved on the server.

Plan: `verse/fairy-forest/README.md`.
acceptance: A planted seed shows a sprout, then grows by real time
Care moves a plant toward its rare form
Reload keeps the garden

tasks.title: Creatures move in and build homes near yours
tasks.body:
Creatures you help can move in near your home: each one picks a plot and builds its own small home, then comes by to visit. The village grows with how much you have helped.

Plan: `verse/fairy-forest/README.md`.
acceptance: A helped creature moves to a plot by your home and builds a house
Its house stays after reload

tasks.title: Timed courses with share links and friends' times
tasks.body:
Build a course of vine hoops with the edit tools, fly it against the clock, and share a link. Friends who open the link fly your course; their best times show on it.

Plan: `verse/fairy-forest/README.md`.
acceptance: A course of hoops times a run from first hoop to last
A share link opens the course for another player
Their best time shows on the course

tasks.title: Learned skills: Speak, Mend, Gather, Craft, Light, Water
tasks.body:
The README's skills table: each skill is learned from its moment (a creature answering, a hurt bird, a first forage, a woodcutter's axe, a night in Lanternwood, clearing the stream) and opens its own help. Skills show as glyphs on screen and are saved.

Plan: `verse/fairy-forest/README.md`.
acceptance: Each of the six skills can be learned from its moment
Learned skills show on screen and stay after reload
